source.title: [AAFLOW+] Stateful Operator Abstraction with Zero-Copy Distributed KV Cache Orchestration for Multi-Agent Workflows
source.summary: Multi-agent LLM systems increasingly integrate retrieval, planning, and reasoning, but remain fundamentally text-centric, requiring agents to repeatedly recompute shared context through expensive prefill. Although single-request inference is known to be accelerated by KV-cache management, it is usually restricted to local serving scopes. We introduce AAFLOW+, a stateful extension of agentic workflow operators that makes KV cache a first-class distributed systems object. AAFLOW+ builds processes into communication-aware graphs that concurrently optimize data, prompts, and reusable model state. It also provides operators for KV materialization, transfer, fork, composition, and eviction. Its runtime enables zero-copy, transfer-aware execution, allowing agents to reuse long context without recomputation. AAFLOW+ reduces TTFT by up to 50.2x, achieves up to 7.63x reduced multi-agent compute cost at 16-agent scale, reduces KV memory by 1.72-6.10x, and increases throughput by more than 7.74x, based on an analytical cost model parameterized by empirical hardware microbenchmarks. The results demonstrate that KV transmission outperforms recomputation on networks with moderate to high bandwidth, making sure KV-state sharing greatly increases efficiency in multi-agent LLM systems by replacing text passing.

previous_facts.title: [AAFLOW+] Stateful Operator Abstraction with Zero-Copy Distributed KV Cache Orchestration for Multi-Agent Workflows
previous_facts.event_hint: AAFLOW+: distributed KV cache orchestration system for multi-agent LLM workflows
previous_facts.problem: Multi-agent LLM systems remain text-centric, requiring downstream agents to repeatedly recompute shared context through expensive prefill even when identical model state was already computed by upstream agents, causing increased TTFT, duplicated computation, and poor branch factor scalability for long-context workloads
previous_facts.mechanism: Stateful operator abstraction extending AAFLOW from dataflow to stateflow, treating KV cache as a first-class distributed systems object with operators for materialization, transfer, fork, restricted composition, and eviction; runtime uses zero-copy communication, Arrow-based formats, explicit metadata, and transfer-aware scheduling to enable efficient KV state transfer between distributed components

previous_facts.evaluation_context: GPU clusters; Mistral-7B and Llama-3-8B models; multi-agent workflows (planner-retriever-solver, tree-of-thought, collaborative RAG); comparison against text-based agent communication; analytical cost model parameterized by empirical hardware microbenchmarks
previous_facts.limitations: Evidence pack contains only abstract/intro/early design (front-evidence-v2); detailed evaluation sections with exact baseline conditions, hardware specifications, network bandwidth parameters, workload configurations, and complete experimental methodology are not visible in current evidence; performance claims are based on analytical cost model parameterized by empirical hardware microbenchmarks; scope focuses on multi-agent workflows rather than single-request optimization; compatibility requirements may limit state reuse (model identity, positional encoding, execution history must match)
previous_facts.project_relevance: Directly addresses TPN questions about state-aware scheduling reducing TTFT/TPOT and KVCache transmission overhead; KV transfer over moderate-to-high bandwidth networks vs recomputation decision criterion (Equation 7) is network-aware; zero-copy distributed KV cache orchestration provides network-side mechanisms beyond pure GPU memory scheduling; project asks whether network perceives KVCache location and Token performance targets—AAFLOW+ makes KV placement and transfer explicit in distributed execution graph
